chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, from Abū Usāmah and Abū Yūsuf Yaʿqūb ibn ʿUthaym, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If a bird, a chicken, or a mouse falls into the well, then draw out seven buckets from it.” We said: “Then what do you say regarding our salat (prayer), our wudu (ablution), and what has affected our clothes?” He said: “There is no problem with it.”

key_terms.الدَّجَاجَةُ: a chicken falling into the well
key_terms.الطَّيْرُ: a bird falling into the well
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which water is drawn
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse falling into the well
key_terms.سَبْعَ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn from the well
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a bird, chicken, or mouse falls into a well, and does it affect salat (prayer), wudu (ablution), or clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a well into which a bird, chicken, or mouse has fallen, instructing that seven buckets be drawn from it. It also clarifies that salat (prayer), wudu (ablution), and clothes previously affected are not considered problematic in this case.
